title: Occupancy-driven launch bundling for FlashAttention + paged KV (rough draft)
body:
Goal
---
Exploratory notes on an occupancy-driven kernel launch bundling strategy that co-schedules FlashAttention invocations and lightweight fused ops while interacting with a paged KV subsystem. Target: reduce tail latency jitter for medium-length sequences (S=256..1024) under mixed workloads, without regressing steady-state throughput.

Context / motivation
- We see two common pressure points in production: (1) variable sequence lengths + KV hits/misses causing uneven GPU SM occupancy and (2) many small FlashAttention launches for short sequences that underutilize warps.
- Paged KV introduces stalls when pages are faulted-in or when eviction cycles kick in; these stalls are often correlated across inflight requests because page granularity is coarse relative to request arrival patterns.
- Idea: dynamically bundle launches (FlashAttn + small fused kernels e.g., rotary/scale*softmax/rownorm) across tokens/requests to keep occupancy high and to hide DMA/prefetch latency from paged KV. Bundle decisions driven by real-time occupancy and pending-page-IO signals.

High-level design
1) Admission layer (runtime scheduler): maintains a short queue of ready attention tasks (A) and small post-attn ops (P). Each task annotated with: seq_len, KV_page_ids_touched, priority, origin (host_id).
2) Occupancy estimator: lightweight GPU-side occupancy model computed from last N kernel execution footprints and current SM free-warp estimate reported by CUDA (via cuOccupancy? or via custom sm counters). Approximates the number of blocks we want to issue per kernel to reach target occupancy (eta).
3) Bundle composer: when either: (a) accumulated ready tasks reach token threshold T_tokens OR (b) time_since_first_ready > T_hold_ms OR (c) predicted occupancy < low_watermark, compose a bundle. Bundle contains up to B_flashattn work items and several P fused ops that can be fused into the same kernel launch.
4) KV-aware prefetcher: before composing a bundle, check KV_page_ids in the set; if missing pages predicted (based on LRU-age + stats), request async page fetch and mark bundle as prefetch-pending. If page fetch latency > budget, the composer may still launch the bundle but with fallback smaller-KV mode (e.g., reroute to smaller local cache or fall back to non-paged path).

Kernel fusion opportunities
- FlashAttention + post-scale + rotary embedding apply: fuse into a single kernel where possible so we avoid extra global mem traffic for Q/K/V postprocessing.
- Small per-token ops (token-weight multiply, local bias add, simple linear projection for reranking) can be appended to tail of attention kernel to amortize launch overhead.
- When bundle contains heterogeneous seq_len, use a two-phase kernel: phase 1 groups tokens into bins by lane-length and runs specialized lane kernels; phase 2 compacts outputs. This reduces divergence and keeps threads busy.

Paged KV interactions (practical heuristics)
- Page grouping: prefer to schedule items touching same page(s) in same bundle to amortize in-flight page fetch. But don't over-group across many origins (isolation).
- Soft quarantine: if an origin has many concurrent page faults, throttle its admission to avoid pumping the page fetcher and starving others.
- Eviction-aware bundling: when eviction pressure high (page walker reports evict cycles), reduce B_flashattn and increase prefetch concurrency to avoid stalling kernels mid-flight.

Microbench pseudocode (conceptual)
- admission queue: deque<task>
- loop:
-    if queue.empty: sleep(poll_ms)
-    sample = queue.peek_window(W)
-    pageset = union(sample.KV_pages)
-    if predicted_page_faults(pageset) > fault_budget:
-       trigger_prefetch(pageset)
-       if time_waited > hold_ms: // fallback or launch with degraded mode
-           compose_bundle(sample, allow_degraded=true)
-    else:
-       compose_bundle(sample)
-    launch_bundle(bundle)

Bundle kernel layout (sketch)
- kernel(bundle_items[], bundle_meta):
-   shared scratch per-block sized by max_seq_len_in_block
-   for item in work assigned to block:
-     load Q/K/V (coalesced) -> shared
-     run flashattn_inner(shared, ...)
-     if post_ops: run fused_post_ops(shared_out)
-     if writes to KV: write-back with CAS/seqnum into page-chunk

Performance safety nets (practical guardrails)
- per-bundle latency SLO: if compose time + estimated execution > per-request SLO, split bundle. Keep worst-case tail controlled.
- autoscale kernel parallelism: if kernel occupies > target_occupancy_high for N windows, reduce B_flashattn to avoid starving other streams.
- metricization: instrument per-bundle: composed_seq_tokens, pages_touched, predicted_fault_count, actual_fault_count, kernel_ms, sm_occupancy_estimate. Send to console for alerting.

Implementation notes / constraints
- Rely on CUDA graph-friendly launches where possible (bundles as replayable graphs) to save launch overhead for repeated bundle shapes. But graphs limit dynamic branching; keep a small set of canonical bundle shapes.
- Use cooperative groups and dynamic shared memory sizing to pack multiple small seqs into a block. Beware of exceeding shared mem limit when max_seq_in_bundle spikes. Consider fallbacks to split block if shared mem overrun.
- Work accounting: we must maintain deterministic per-request metrics for billing and debugging. Keep mapping from request -> bundle_id and record offsets.

Open questions / experiments to run
- What is the right token threshold T_tokens as function of S distribution? Run param sweep: T_tokens in {64, 256, 512, 1024} on mixed workload (40% S=64, 40% S=512, 20% S=1024).
- Evaluate occupancy estimator accuracy: compare CUDA occupancy API vs. sm-level counters sampled by perf kernels. How often can/should we sample (cost vs. benefit)?
- Prefetch budget tuning: How many concurrent page fetches are optimal before diminishing returns or causing PCIe saturation? Use synthetic experiments with varying page sizes (4KB chunks vs. 64KB chunks) and different NVMe throughput models.
- Fused vs multi-launch tradeoff: microbench fused kernel latency vs two-launch (FlashAttn + post-op) across seq lengths. For very short seqs fusion helps; for long seqs fusion can increase register pressure. Need empirical register pressure/warp-occupancy curves.

Short TODOs
- [ ] Prototype bundle composer shim (host-side) and a minimal fused kernel using existing FlashAttn inner loop (Maya)
- [ ] Add per-bundle telemetry to tracing pipeline (Priya)
- [ ] Small bench matrix: vary T_tokens, B_flashattn, hold_ms on dev cluster (Diego)
- [ ] Simulate paged-KV page-faults using mock slowback (Liam)

Risks and mitigations
- Increased code complexity: start behind a runtime flag and roll out to low-traffic region first. Keep simple fallback to single-request launches.
- Regression on worst-case latency for high-priority requests: allow priority bypass so high-SLA requests get immediate isolated bundles.
- Hard-to-debug inter-request fusion effects (data leaks, owner isolation): maintain strict zero-copy boundaries and per-request memory fences; record explicit request->bundle mapping for replay.

Notes to self
- Prototype should aim to be non-invasive: minimal changes to FlashAttn inner loop, host-side composer as separate module. Keep early experiments off in Dedicated to avoid noisy neighbor issues.
- Consider integrating with existing autoscaler signals so that when bundling increases effective occupancy we can reduce number of active SM partitions or adjust per-tenant weight.

Appendix: quick benchmark plan
- workloads: synth-short (S=32..128), synth-med (S=256..512), synth-mixed (40/40/20), chat-like traces replayed from prod trace sample.
- metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency per-request, tokens/sec, kernel-sm-occupancy, page-fault-rate, number-of-prefetches, PCIe throughput.
- baseline: existing per-request FlashAttn launches + current paged-KV prefetch heuristics.
- targets: reduce p99 latency by 10-20% on mixed workload while keeping tokens/sec +/-5% of baseline.

End.
